topic: Natural modes of an ideal stretched string
problem: Find the frequencies of natural oscillations of a steel string with a length of l=50 cm and a diameter of d=1 mm if the tension of the string is T=2450 dynes. The density of steel is ρ=7.8 g/cm³.
solution: The supplied solution states ν=ν₀ n for n=1,2,3,... and ν₀=(1/(l d))√(T/(πρ))=2 s⁻¹, hence νₙ=2n s⁻¹.
solution_assumptions: Ideal uniform stretched-string modes with both ends fixed are the model interpretation of the supplied harmonic law; damping and bending stiffness are omitted.
source_solution_audit: With the stated values and exact Real.pi, f₁=√(490/(39π)), rigorously 1.9998<f₁<1.9999 Hz, so it is not exactly 2. Neither π=22/7 nor π=3.14 makes f₁ exactly 2. No hidden source choice of π is asserted. The formalization adopts nearest-whole-Hz rounding as an explicit interpretation of the printed integer answer.
formal_interpretation: Given the source-native string data and local circular cross-section, return the unique positive-mode frequency family agreeing with the reusable ideal FixedString model. The trusted target contains neither the combined formula nor a numerical answer. Candidate constructs fₙ=n√(490/(39π)) after deriving the cylindrical formula from the reusable mode law and specializing the source data. Separate Candidate theorems certify 1.9998<f₁<1.9999 Hz and whole-Hz rounding to 2; |fₙ−2n|<n/5000 Hz is an approximation bound, not an exact equality or an all-mode nearest-integer rounding claim. Units checks native CGS conversion, SI conversion and dimensions.
